title: design-parity config
description: Committed, per-repo parity policy (`.design-parity.json`), read deterministically by the bot. Setup materializes a concrete direction; `auto` is only the pre-setup default. See docs/PRINCIPLES.md, Principle 5.

$comment.description: Free-text rationale for the settings below, ignored by the bot. JSON has no comment syntax and `$comment` is the JSON Schema annotation keyword for exactly this; rejecting it pushed repos into deleting the reasoning for their own direction (yschimke/m3-catalog#11).

direction.description: Who is canonical when design and code disagree. 'design-led' blocks the PR on a violation (fix is in code); 'code-led' makes violations advisory and allows pushing drift back to the design tool; 'auto' is a transitional default that setup materializes — and the Action resolves as a late fallback — into a concrete direction from the repo's maturity rung.

cmpCapable.description: Whether the repo is Compose Multiplatform capable (Principle 6). Recorded by setup/bootstrap from its deterministic CMP scan so the unattended Action can promote CMP to Android-only repos without re-deriving it per run (Principle 1). false ⇒ Android-only (the PR comment carries a non-blocking 'could run faster on CMP' suggestion); true ⇒ already CMP; omitted ⇒ setup hasn't recorded it. Advisory only — never a gate.

tokens.description: Token-comparison policy: what this platform can be held to, as opposed to how close it has to be. Tolerances stay committed engine defaults (Principle 1) and are deliberately not settable here.

missingNumerics.description: What a numeric spec token the candidate resolves NO value for is worth. 'advisory' (default) reports it as a non-blocking note, on the same 'we can't verify, so we don't accuse' reasoning already applied when a candidate resolves a whole token group of nothing; 'strict' restores the hard error that forces a Fail. A value the candidate does report is compared strictly either way. Wear is the worked example: a component inset by touchTargetAwareSize plus a sized child declares no padding modifier, and adding one to clear the check would misrepresent how the library composes (issue #368).

textDerivedInsets.description: Whether an inset MEASURED off a text child counts as padding. The derived-inset check reads the gap between a container and its children — a sound proxy for padding when the child is a box, and font metrics when it is a glyph. 'skip' (default) drops such a measurement rather than quoting it against a declared padding; 'measure' reports it like any other (issue #367).

acceptedDifferences.description: Exact, issue-backed token divergences that cannot currently be expressed by the platform. Every identity and value must still match; drift remains blocking.
